articles.title: Report: More US troops have died in Iran war than Pentagon says
articles.summary: The Pentagon publicly lists 18 US military deaths since the Iran war began.
articles.body:
Report: More US troops have died in Iran war than Pentagon says

The Pentagon publicly lists 18 US military deaths since the Iran war began. But, The Washington Post has cited six unnamed Pentagon officials who say the toll is at least 22. The Pentagon has declined to explain the discrepancy and Pete Hegseth has called the report ‘a complete lie’.

articles.summary: Semana de Artes Visuais do Recife chega à 11ª edição a partir deste sábado (19). Atividades seguem até 27 de setembro. Entre as atrações, estão Ava Rocha e a banda Metá Metá.
articles.body:
Semana de Artes Visuais do Recife, o SPA das Artes, promove intervenções artísticas na cidade — Foto: Andréa Rêgo Barros/PCR

A Semana de Artes Visuais do Recife , o SPA das Artes, retorna às ruas da capital pernambucana a partir deste sábado (19), com mais de 40 atividades gratuitas, incluindo shows, intervenções artísticas, rodas de conversa, Mostra de Videoarte e atrações do Salão Recife de Artes Visuais. A programação conta com a participação de artistas de todo o Brasil (veja programação abaixo) .

A 11ª edição do evento, realizado pela prefeitura do Recife, segue até 27 de setembro e homenageará artistas que integram a história do SPA das Artes: Fernando Augusto, Fernando Duarte, José Paulo, Mauricio Castro e Rinaldo Silva, criadores do evento, além de Christina Machado, artista plástica paraense radicada em Pernambuco.

A abertura oficial do evento começa às 16h, no Pátio de São Pedro, no bairro de São José, no Centro do Recife. No evento, haverá o lançamento do Mapa das Artes, plataforma digital de mapeamento dos espaços culturais da cidade. Além disso, o público poderá apreciar a Mostra SPA de Videoarte. A cerimônia conta, ainda, com um show da banda paulista Metá Metá.

Durante os nove dias de evento, o SPA das Artes também traz shows das pernambucanas DJ Vibra e DJ IDLibra, da compositora e cineasta carioca Ava Rocha e da DJ IDLibra, todos no Pátio de São Pedro.

Já as performances, intervenções e instalações de rua poderão ser vistas em diveros espaços abertos, incluindo praças, parques e pontes. Na programação, destacam-se as pinturas dos murais “Raiz Nordestina” e “Cacheiro viajante, cuando muda o tempo”.

Para as crianças, o “SPAzinho das Artes” levará ao bairro de Casa Amarela, na Zona Norte do Recife, uma imersão artístico-educativa entre os dias 20 e 27, com oficina, aula de campo e exposição coletiva.

A Mostra Videoarte trará exibições itinerantes na Praça do Sebo, no bairro de Santo Antônio, no Centro do Recife, além do Museu Murillo La Greca, no bairro do Parnamirim, na Zona Norte do Recife, e do Museu de Arte Moderna Aloisio Magalhães (Mamam), na Boa Vista.

articles.title: Notícias do Triângulo: granizo, castelo de 17 metros e órgãos doados | G1
articles.standfirst: Resumo de notícias da semana entre os dias 12 e 18 de setembro.
articles.summary: O resumo das notícias do Triângulo Mineiro destaca o granizo em Araxá, o castelo construído em Uberlândia e um emocionante relato sobre doação de órgãos.
articles.body:
Confira o que foi destaque no g1 Triângulo nesta semana, com as notícias mais acessadas entre os dias 12 a 18 de setembro.

Araxá ficou coberta por uma camada de granizo durante uma chuva registrada na segunda-feira (14). Vídeos feitos durante o temporal mostram uma grande quantidade de pedras de gelo acumuladas no chão.

Em um dos vídeos, uma rodovia aparece praticamente coberta pelo granizo, deixando o asfalto escondido sob uma camada de gelo. Veja acima.

Mais do que o tamanho das pedras, a quantidade chama atenção nas imagens. Segundo o geógrafo William Borges, uma frente fria que atuava sobre o Sudeste aumentou a umidade na região e criou condições favoráveis à formação de tempestades.

A ideia era construir apenas uma guarita, em formato de castelo, para reforçar a segurança da chácara de Juliano Braga, de 68 anos, em Uberlândia . Mas, à medida que as paredes subiam, a construção também crescia. O que deveria ser uma estrutura pequena acabou se transformando em um castelo de cerca de 17 metros de altura no bairro Mansões Aeroporto.

Piloto executivo aposentado, Juliano conta que a inspiração veio de uma paixão antiga por história e das viagens que fez à França para visitar a filha, Caroline Braga, que mora no país e tem três filhos. Durante as visitas, conheceu diferentes castelos e guardou na memória elementos da arquitetura medieval.

“Eu sempre fui apaixonado por história. No colégio, eu sempre gostei disso. Aí minha filha mudou para a França, casou com francês e visitei a França algumas vezes e fui em alguns castelos”, contou.

O resultado foi uma construção personalizada, inspirada em elementos que Juliano viu em castelos europeus. Há torres pontiagudas, arcos, escadas em espiral e janelas desenhadas especialmente para o imóvel. Segundo ele, as torres foram feitas com estruturas metálicas para evitar excesso de peso.

A construção começou em 2020 e ficou pronta por volta de 2024. Por dentro, o espaço ganhou cozinha, banheiro social, uma suíte e outros ambientes, mas não segue necessariamente o estilo medieval do exterior.

Lilian e Adriano ficaram casados por 31 anos e tiveram 3 filhos. — Foto: Adriano Duarte /Arquivo Pessoal

Depois de 31 anos ao lado da esposa, o técnico de projetos Adriano Duarte da Silva, de 53 anos, precisou tomar uma decisão difícil: autorizar a doação dos órgãos dela. Lílian Raquel Duarte da Silva tinha 49 anos quando faleceu, vítima de um AVC hemorrágico, em janeiro de 2024, em Araxá.

Com a autorização de Adriano, as córneas e os rins dela foram doados. Segundo ele, nunca havia conversado com a mulher sobre o assunto, mas decidiu permitir a doação porque sabia o quanto ela gostava de ajudar outras pessoas.

Adriano lembra que o problema de saúde da esposa começou em 11 de dezembro de 2024 quando Lílian estava na igreja, onde dava aulas de crisma e passou mal.

“Ela sentiu uma forte dor de cabeça e perdeu os movimentos do corpo. Eu, imediatamente levei ela para o hospital, mas o problema não foi identificado naquele momento. Nos dias seguintes, ela continuou apresentando mal-estar”, contou.

Na noite de 1º de janeiro, Lílian foi para o quarto mais cedo. Pouco depois, acabou caindo no chão.

Adriano prestou os primeiros socorros e ela foi levada novamente para o hospital. Desta vez, não voltou para casa.

articles.standfirst: Chamada Pública define regras para eleição das instituições que irão compor o Conselho no biênio 2027-2028.
articles.summary: Chamada Pública define regras para eleição das instituições que irão compor o Conselho no biênio 2027-2028.
articles.body:
A eleição será realizada durante a 6ª Conferência de Desenvolvimento Rural Sustentável — Foto: Secom

A Secretaria Municipal de Pesca e Agropecuária de Rio das Ostras publicou a Chamada Pública nº 001/2026, que estabelece as regras para o processo eleitoral do Conselho Municipal de Desenvolvimento Rural Sustentável e Pesca (CMDRSP) para o biênio 2027-2028.

A eleição será realizada durante a 6ª Conferência Municipal de Desenvolvimento Rural Sustentável e Pesca e definirá as instituições que irão ocupar as 12 vagas destinadas ao Plenário do Conselho. O mandato ordinário dos novos representantes será exercido de 30 de novembro de 2026 a 29 de novembro de 2028.

O processo é conduzido pela Comissão Organizadora da 6ª Conferência Municipal de Desenvolvimento Rural Sustentável e Pesca, instituída pela Portaria nº 002/2026 – SEPAGRO. O CMDRSP foi criado pela Lei Municipal nº 627, de 7 de março de 2002, e tem entre suas atribuições a participação e o acompanhamento das políticas relacionadas ao Desenvolvimento Rural Sustentável e à pesca no Município.

VAGAS – Do total de 12 vagas, oito serão destinadas a instituições representantes da sociedade civil organizada. Para participar, as organizações devem ter sede em Rio das Ostras, estar constituídas há pelo menos dois anos antes da Conferência Municipal e comprovar atuação no Município nas áreas de pesca e/ou agropecuária.

INSCRIÇÕES – Após o encerramento do período de inscrições, a Comissão Organizadora divulgará a relação das instituições habilitadas. O regulamento também estabelece prazos específicos para apresentação de impugnações e recursos, julgamento e divulgação da lista final de habilitados.

Todas as datas, locais e demais informações referentes às etapas do processo eleitoral estão disponíveis no Anexo IV da Chamada Pública.

ELEIÇÃO E POSSE – O fórum eleitoral será realizado durante a 6ª Conferência Municipal de Desenvolvimento Rural Sustentável e Pesca de Rio das Ostras, em data e local definidos no regulamento. A eleição dos membros do CMDRSP seguirá as normas previstas no Regimento Interno da Conferência, que será apresentado e submetido à aprovação durante o evento.

Após a eleição, os representantes indicados pelas instituições vencedoras serão empossados pelo presidente do Conselho/secretário municipal de Pesca e Agropecuária, conforme o cronograma estabelecido na Chamada Pública.

articles.title: Discord mantém brecha para transmissões ao vivo no Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: A GloboNews identificou ferramentas dentro do próprio aplicativo que permitem compartilhar tela e imagens em tempo real. Após ser informada, ANPD notificou a empresa e alertou para possibilidade de multa diária.
articles.summary: A GloboNews identificou ferramentas dentro do próprio aplicativo que permitem compartilhar tela e imagens em tempo real. Após ser informada, ANPD notificou a empresa.
articles.body:
O Discord continua permitindo que usuários no Brasil utilizem serviços que possibilitam a transmissão de vídeo em tempo real e o compartilhamento de tela. A brecha foi identificada mais de um mês após a Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD) determinar a suspensão imediata de todas as transmissões ao vivo na plataforma no Brasil.

A GloboNews encontrou pelo menos duas ferramentas disponíveis na seção nativa de "atividades" do Discord que seguem plenamente funcionais para usuários brasileiros, sem qualquer restrição técnica ou bloqueio geográfico aparente. Os recursos permitem o espelhamento de tela e a exibição de imagens em tempo real durante chamadas de voz e em servidores.

Por questões de segurança e para evitar facilitar o acesso às ferramentas por infratores, a reportagem optou por não divulgar seus nomes nem o passo a passo para ativá-las.

Procurada, a ANPD informou que, a partir dos dados apresentados pela GloboNews , pediu esclarecimentos ao Discord e alertou que o descumprimento de medidas preventivas pode acarretar sanções, incluindo a aplicação de multa diária. (leia a nota abaixo)

'Suspensão vira fachada', diz especialista

Os recursos identificados operam por meio do ecossistema de desenvolvedores do próprio aplicativo.

Um dos serviços chega a exibir um aviso em inglês antes de ser iniciado, em que o usuário precisa marcar que "entende que este recurso não tem a intenção de burlar restrições regionais ou bloqueio geográfico" e que "apenas adiciona suporte a compartilhamento de tela". Na prática, porém, o vídeo é transmitido normalmente na sala.

Para David Nemer, antropólogo da tecnologia e professor da Universidade da Virgínia, a existência dessas ferramentas compromete a eficácia da medida adotada no Brasil.

"As atividades são aplicativos que rodam dentro do próprio Discord, construídos com o kit de desenvolvimento da empresa e abertos em uma vitrine que ela controla", avalia Nemer.

"Se uma dessas atividades entrega exatamente o que a ANPD mandou suspender, que é a tela ao vivo em sala fechada, a suspensão vira fachada. Se a porta foi aberta de propósito ou ficou esquecida, pouco importa: a responsabilidade é do Discord."

O pesquisador ressalta que a brecha mantém os riscos que motivaram a suspensão inicial. "O risco está na combinação de vídeo ao vivo, sala fechada, público selecionado e moderação fraca. Uma atividade de compartilhamento de tela em sala com senha reproduz essa combinação por inteiro. Para quem alicia e chantageia adolescentes, o nome do botão é irrelevante", diz.

"Há até um agravante: se o vídeo passa por servidores de terceiros, a plataforma enxerga ainda menos do que enxergava na live original. A vulnerabilidade exposta pela Operação Lívia continua aberta, agora com um carimbo de 'cumprimos a ordem', quando na verdade não cumpriram."

A determinação da ANPD, publicada em 12 de agosto, teve como estopim uma investigação sobre a morte de uma adolescente de 13 anos em Mato Grosso do Sul , no fim de julho. Segundo as autoridades policiais, a jovem morreu durante uma transmissão de vídeo ao vivo no Discord.

As apurações apontam que ela foi induzida ao suicídio por criminosos que mantinham contato com ela em servidores fechados, em um esquema classificado pelos investigadores como "escravidão digital".

Nesse modelo de coação, os suspeitos se aproximavam de vítimas em situação de vulnerabilidade, simulavam amizade e confiança para, em seguida, fazer ameaças, extorsões e exigir desafios violentos — que incluíam automutilação e maus-tratos a animais — até chegar ao desfecho fatal.

O caso deu origem à Operação Lívia, deflagrada pela Polícia Civil e pelo Ministério da Justiça, que nesta semana apreendeu seis adolescentes suspeitos de integrar a rede criminosa em quatro estados e no Distrito Federal.

A decisão regulatória se apoia nas diretrizes do Estatuto da Criança e do Adolescente Digital (ECA Digital), em vigor desde 17 de março deste ano . A legislação ampliou os deveres das empresas de tecnologia cujos serviços têm acesso provável de crianças e adolescentes no país.

Pela nova regra, as plataformas são obrigadas a adotar salvaguardas ativas contra conteúdos ilegais, abuso sexual, automutilação, drogas e violência, além de implementar sistemas eficazes de verificação de faixa etária e ferramentas obrigatórias de controle parental.

O descumprimento das normas do ECA Digital sujeita as empresas a sanções administrativas que vão de multas até a suspensão temporária das atividades no país.

Depois de live que terminou em morte, Discord suspende transmissões ao vivo no país — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Procurada pela GloboNews , a Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD) enviou a seguinte nota.

"A Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD) informa que, a partir da denúncia recebida, já solicitou ao Discord esclarecimentos sobre o conteúdo apresentado pela GloboNews. O descumprimento de medidas preventivas pode gerar a imposição de novas medidas, como, por exemplo, a aplicação de multa diária.

A Superintendência de Fiscalização (SFI-ANPD) decidiu manter a interrupção temporária das transmissões ao vivo do Discord ao indeferir o pedido de efeito suspensivo da medida preventiva apresentado no recurso da plataforma, por entender que a retomada das lives e do compartilhamento de vídeos ao vivo, sem a adoção de medidas que tornem essa funcionalidade mais segura para crianças e adolescentes, poderia gerar risco de repetição das condutas investigadas e de novos danos antes mesmo da conclusão do processo de fiscalização, que segue em curso desde o dia 07/08.

A área técnica reforça que a suspensão das transmissões ao vivo tem caráter temporário e sua reversão continua condicionada à demonstração, pelo Discord, da implementação de salvaguardas capazes de mitigar os riscos identificados, sem impedir a continuidade das demais funcionalidades da plataforma. A empresa e a SFI seguem em diálogo sobre as medidas a serem implementadas para garantir a proteção de crianças e adolescentes.

O mérito dos demais itens do recurso do Discord foi analisado pela SFI e seguiu, na última quinta-feira (17), para o Conselho Diretor da ANPD, instância responsável por decidir o recurso em caráter final na via administrativa."

A GloboNews também procurou a assessoria de imprensa do Discord para saber por que as ferramentas de vídeo permanecem acessíveis no Brasil e quais providências serão tomadas. A empresa não respondeu até a publicação desta reportagem.

articles.title: Fim de semana terá temporais no Sul e avanço da chuva para o Sudeste | G1
articles.standfirst: Formação de uma área de baixa pressão entre o Paraguai e o Sul do Brasil aumenta o risco de temporais no Sul e favorece o avanço da chuva para áreas do Sudeste.
articles.summary: Formação de uma área de baixa pressão entre o Paraguai e o Sul do Brasil aumenta o risco de temporais no Sul e favorece o avanço da chuva para áreas do Sudeste.
articles.body:
Chuva no RS — Foto: Jeff Botega/Agência RBS

O último fim de semana do inverno será marcado por uma mudança no tempo em boa parte do país.

➡️A formação de uma área de baixa pressão entre o Paraguai e o Sul do Brasil aumenta o risco de temporais no Sul e favorece o avanço da chuva para áreas do Sudeste .

Ao longo da sexta (18), o tempo já voltou a ficar instável em parte dessas regiões, especialmente no Sul.

Segundo o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet), a mudança está ligada a uma nova configuração da atmosfera, com o enfraquecimento do canal de umidade que vinha atuando sobre outras áreas do país.

Com essa transformação, o Jato de Baixos Níveis — uma corrente de vento que transporta ar quente e úmido de áreas mais ao norte em direção ao Sul — se intensifica.

➡️O aumento da umidade e a queda da pressão atmosférica favorecem a formação de novas áreas de instabilidade e o retorno das chuvas à região .

A chuva ganha força entre sábado (19) e domingo (20) no Sul, com possibilidade de temporais, raios, ventos fortes e granizo.

No domingo, a formação de um ciclone extratropical próximo à costa do Rio Grande do Sul aumenta a instabilidade.

Já no Centro-Oeste, o cenário é dividido: enquanto Mato Grosso, Goiás e o Distrito Federal continuam com calor intenso e baixa umidade, Mato Grosso do Sul terá aumento da chuva, principalmente no sul do estado.

No Nordeste, as pancadas ficam concentradas na faixa leste, enquanto o interior segue quente e seco e, no Norte, a chuva continua mais presente no oeste, com calor predominando nas demais áreas.

Veja abaixo, em detalhes, como fica a previsão para cada região.

⛈️Sábado (19) - área de baixa pressão entre o Paraguai e o Sul do Brasil aumenta a instabilidade

A chuva ganha força no oeste, noroeste e norte do Rio Grande do Sul, no oeste e em grande parte de Santa Catarina e no sul e sudoeste do Paraná.

São esperadas pancadas de moderadas a fortes, acompanhadas de raios, rajadas de vento e possibilidade de temporais . Os maiores volumes devem se concentrar no oeste de Santa Catarina, além do oeste, sudoeste e sul do Paraná e de áreas do norte, oeste e noroeste gaúcho.

No sul do Rio Grande do Sul, na Campanha e no litoral, ainda haverá períodos de sol entre nuvens, mas não estão descartadas pancadas de chuva. As rajadas podem chegar a 90 km/h em pontos isolados .

🌀Domingo (20) - formação de um ciclone extratropical próximo à costa gaúcha

O sistema favorece chuva forte, temporais, raios, ventos intensos e possibilidade de granizo.

A chuva continua intensa em Santa Catarina, no centro-sul e leste do estado, no norte do Paraná e em diferentes áreas do Rio Grande do Sul. O sudoeste gaúcho terá melhora gradual.

Há possibilidade de volumes elevados de chuva na região central do Rio Grande do Sul. No Paraná, a preocupação aumenta porque o solo já está encharcado, o que pode favorecer novos alagamentos e deslizamentos.

☁️Sábado (19) - instabilidade em parte da região

A umidade vinda do oceano mantém muitas nuvens e chuva fraca a moderada no litoral de São Paulo, no Rio de Janeiro, na Zona da Mata e no leste e nordeste de Minas Gerais, além do sul do Espírito Santo.

No interior paulista, Triângulo Mineiro e oeste de Minas, o tempo fica mais aberto e quente. Entre a tarde e a noite, porém, a atuação da baixa pressão favorece pancadas no oeste, noroeste, sul, sudoeste, litoral sul e centro de São Paulo, além do Triângulo Mineiro.

Há risco de temporais no sul, extremo oeste e sudoeste paulista.

🌧️Domingo (20) - a chuva aumenta em São Paulo

As pancadas começam já pela manhã no oeste, sudoeste, sul e centro do estado e avançam para outras áreas ao longo do dia. Os temporais podem ocorrer principalmente perto da divisa com o Paraná.

No Rio de Janeiro, o dia começa mais firme, mas a nebulosidade aumenta à tarde, com possibilidade de chuva isolada na Costa Verde e no sul do estado.

Sul de Minas e parte da Zona da Mata também voltam a ter chuva moderada a forte, com risco de temporais no extremo sul mineiro. No Espírito Santo, o interior continua quente e seco, enquanto o litoral terá mais nuvens.

Centro-Oeste: calor continua, mas MS terá chuva

🌡️Sábado (19) - calor e baixa umidade continuam

Mato Grosso continua com temperaturas muito elevadas e baixa umidade, principalmente no centro-leste. Goiás e o Distrito Federal também terão calor e baixa umidade em parte da região.

Em Mato Grosso do Sul, principalmente no sul, sudoeste e oeste, a aproximação da baixa pressão aumenta a nebulosidade e favorece pancadas de chuva, especialmente entre a tarde e a noite. A chuva avança para áreas centrais e leste do estado e para o sul de Goiás.

Há risco de temporais e chuva volumosa no extremo sul de Mato Grosso do Sul. No oeste e sudoeste de Mato Grosso, o calor e a umidade favorecem pancadas de moderadas a fortes.

🌦️Domingo (20) - calor e chuva forte no Mato Grosso do Sul

A chuva moderada a forte continua no extremo sul e leste de Mato Grosso do Sul, com possibilidade de granizo.

Em Goiás e no Distrito Federal, predominam o calor e as pancadas isoladas. Também pode chover de forma localizada no oeste de Mato Grosso.

As temperaturas permanecem elevadas, enquanto a umidade segue baixa em grande parte de Mato Grosso e Goiás. Em algumas áreas do sul e sudeste mato-grossenses, os índices podem ficar entre 12% e 20%.

Nordeste: chuva no litoral e tempo seco no interior

🌧️Sábado (19) - pancadas de chuva na faixa litorânea

As pancadas de chuva atingem principalmente a faixa entre o litoral do Rio Grande do Norte e Sergipe, além de pontos do litoral do Maranhão.

Na Bahia, a aproximação de uma frente fria favorece chuva entre o Recôncavo Baiano e Ilhéus, com risco de temporais. No interior, o tempo continua quente e seco, com umidade entre 12% e 20% no sul do Piauí e do Maranhão.

🌦️Domingo (20) - chuva continua concentrada na faixa leste

Os maiores volumes são esperados entre o litoral norte da Bahia, o Recôncavo Baiano e Salvador.

Também há previsão de pancadas moderadas a fortes entre o litoral do Rio Grande do Norte e Sergipe. No interior da Bahia, Pernambuco, Piauí, Ceará e em outras áreas do sertão, o tempo segue seco e quente, com temperaturas próximas dos 38°C.

🌧️Sábado (19) - chuvas isoladas em parte da região

A chuva permanece mais concentrada no oeste, norte e centro do Amazonas, oeste de Roraima, sul de Rondônia e pontos do litoral do Pará. As pancadas podem ser moderadas a fortes, com possibilidade de temporais.

Acre e norte de Rondônia também podem ter chuva isolada. Nas demais áreas, o tempo fica seco, com poucas nuvens e temperaturas elevadas.

🌦️Domingo (20) - pancadas em alguns locais e calor continuam

As pancadas continuam principalmente no oeste e norte do Amazonas, no Acre e no oeste de Roraima. Também pode chover entre o sul do Amazonas e o norte de Rondônia e no noroeste e oeste do Pará.

No restante da região, o tempo permanece firme, quente e seco. As temperaturas podem se aproximar dos 40°C no Tocantins, sudeste do Pará e leste do Amazonas.

articles.title: Quase metade fingiu estar ocupada para evitar trabalho, diz pesquisa | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento com 2.487 profissionais mostra que 69,4% já procuraram outro emprego sem avisar o empregador, e 48,6% dizem já ter fingido estar ocupados para evitar novas tarefas.
articles.summary: Levantamento com 2.487 profissionais mostra que 69,4% já procuraram outro emprego sem avisar o empregador, e 48,6% dizem já ter fingido estar ocupados para evitar novas tarefas.
articles.body:
Quase metade dos profissionais admite fingir estar ocupada para evitar mais trabalho, diz levantamento — Foto: Reprodução/Freepik

Uma pesquisa nacional realizada pela Heach Recursos Humanos revelou que 48,6% dos profissionais disseram já ter fingido estar ocupados para evitar receber novas demandas de trabalho.

O levantamento ouviu 2.487 profissionais de diferentes segmentos e investigou comportamentos ligados à produtividade, à busca por novas oportunidades, à gestão do tempo durante o expediente, a faltas e às informações apresentadas em currículos.

Segundo a pesquisa, 86,5% dos entrevistados disseram já ter adotado pelo menos um dos oito comportamentos analisados, que, em geral, passam despercebidos pelas empresas.

O comportamento mais frequente foi a busca por outro emprego sem comunicar a empresa atual . Segundo os dados, 69,4% dos entrevistados afirmaram já ter feito isso de forma discreta, o equivalente a 1.726 pessoas da amostra.

Em seguida, 66,8% disseram já ter resolvido assuntos pessoais durante o horário de trabalho. Outros 54,7% relataram ter participado de entrevistas para outras vagas durante o expediente.

Entre os comportamentos relacionados ao uso do tempo de trabalho, 51,2% disseram já ter informado que estavam trabalhando quando, na realidade, realizavam alguma atividade pessoal.

Já 48,6% afirmaram ter fingido estar ocupados para evitar receber novas tarefas, o equivalente a 1.209 pessoas.

Veja os principais resultados da pesquisa:

🔎 69,4% já procuraram outro emprego sem informar a empresa;

😐 66,8% resolveram assuntos pessoais durante o expediente;

👩🏽‍💻 54,7% fizeram entrevista para outro emprego durante o horário de trabalho;

💻 51,2% disseram estar trabalhando enquanto realizavam uma atividade pessoal;

🚨 48,6% fingiram estar ocupados para evitar receber mais trabalho;

⏰ 39,7% inventaram ou exageraram uma justificativa para atraso ou ausência;

🤧 33,6% utilizaram atestado mesmo considerando que poderiam trabalhar;

📃 29,4% mentiram, omitiram ou exageraram alguma informação no currículo.

Comportamento dos trabalhadores oculto das empresas — Foto: Arte g1

O levantamento, batizado de "A Vida Secreta do Trabalhador Brasileiro", aponta comportamentos que podem não aparecer nos indicadores tradicionais usados pelas empresas para acompanhar a rotina dos funcionários.

Para Elcio Teixeira, CEO da Heach, os resultados devem ser analisados de maneiras diferentes e não representam necessariamente um retrato de "maus funcionários".

"Não podemos colocar no mesmo lugar alguém que procura outra oportunidade profissional e alguém que falseia uma informação no currículo. São fenômenos completamente diferentes", afirma.

Segundo o executivo, os resultados mostram uma diferença entre aquilo que as empresas conseguem acompanhar por meio de sistemas e indicadores e o que ocorre na rotina dos funcionários.

“As empresas sabem muito sobre seus funcionários do ponto de vista cadastral, contratual e de desempenho, mas sabem muito menos sobre o que acontece na relação cotidiana entre indivíduo e trabalho", explica.

"Quando 86,5% dos profissionais reconhecem pelo menos um comportamento que permanece fora do radar da organização, talvez o dado mais importante não seja a transgressão, mas a dimensão dessa zona invisível na relação de trabalho", completa o executivo.

Faltas, atestados e informações em currículos

A pesquisa também identificou comportamentos relacionados a faltas, atestados e informações apresentadas em processos seletivos.

Entre os entrevistados, 39,7% disseram já ter inventado ou exagerado uma justificativa para atrasos ou ausências. Outros 33,6% afirmaram ter usado atestado médico mesmo acreditando que tinham condições de exercer suas atividades.

Já 29,4% reconheceram ter omitido, exagerado ou apresentado informações incorretas no currículo durante processos seletivos.

Para Teixeira, os resultados também levantam questionamentos sobre modelos de gestão baseados principalmente na presença, na disponibilidade ou no tempo de conexão.

"Quanto maior a distância entre aquilo que as pessoas fazem e aquilo que sentem que podem dizer à organização, maior é o ponto cego da gestão", afirma.

O executivo também considera que buscar uma nova oportunidade profissional sem comunicar a empresa faz parte da autonomia do trabalhador e, por si só, não configura irregularidade.

Esses comportamentos podem afetar a relação profissional?

Os resultados, por si só, não permitem concluir que os trabalhadores estejam insatisfeitos ou desengajados , mas revelam uma distância entre o que vivem no ambiente de trabalho e o que sentem que podem expor à empresa.

Para Louis Burlamaqui, especialista em cultura organizacional, o número de profissionais que admitem esconder determinados comportamentos chama atenção e pode indicar um problema de confiança nas relações de trabalho.

“Eu não diria que 86,5% das pessoas estão desengajadas. Mas diria que existe uma distância relevante entre aquilo que o trabalhador vive e aquilo que sente que pode revelar dentro da empresa”, afirma.

Um dos resultados que mais chamaram atenção foi a percepção de sobrecarga velada : quase metade dos entrevistados afirmou já ter aparentado estar ocupada para não receber novas demandas.

Segundo Burlamaqui, o comportamento pode funcionar como uma estratégia informal de proteção diante da dificuldade de estabelecer limites de forma direta.

Segundo ele, em algumas organizações, profissionais mais eficientes acabam recebendo novas demandas de forma contínua, o que pode incentivar mecanismos silenciosos de defesa.

A pesquisa também mostra que procurar outro emprego sem comunicar a empresa é um comportamento comum. Para Burlamaqui, buscar oportunidades no mercado é um movimento natural da carreira e não significa, necessariamente, insatisfação com o emprego atual.

Quando essa procura se torna recorrente, porém, pode estar relacionada a fatores como remuneração, perspectivas de crescimento, reconhecimento ou relação com a liderança.

Embora essas atitudes possam ser pontuais, Burlamaqui alerta que podem trazer consequências quando se transformam em padrão.

“A reputação profissional é construída pela consistência dos comportamentos. Existe uma diferença importante entre estabelecer limites e fugir de responsabilidades”, ressalta.

Como alternativa, ele defende conversas mais transparentes entre trabalhadores e gestores sobre capacidade de entrega, prioridades e carga de trabalho. “Tenho estas cinco entregas e entrou uma sexta. Qual delas deve perder prioridade?”, exemplifica.

Para o especialista, as empresas também precisam criar ambientes em que os profissionais possam falar sobre limites e dificuldades sem receio de consequências negativas. “Quando a conversa formal não funciona, o comportamento informal acaba ocupando esse espaço”, conclui.

A pesquisa ouviu profissionais das cinco regiões do país entre 1º e 11 de setembro de 2026. Os participantes foram selecionados a partir da base da Heach Recursos Humanos, que reúne mais de 14 milhões de currículos, e responderam a um questionário estruturado e autoadministrado em ambiente digital.

A amostra buscou contemplar diferenças de idade, escolaridade, região, nível hierárquico e modelo de trabalho. Para cada um dos oito comportamentos investigados, os participantes podiam responder “sim”, “não” ou “prefiro não responder”.

Segundo a empresa, os resultados se referem apenas aos participantes do levantamento e devem ser interpretados considerando que a amostra foi formada a partir da base de profissionais da própria Heach.

articles.title: MHA cites internal security issues to defend FCRA tweak
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Amid the charge from the opposition that Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill targets institutions run by minorities, especiall.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Amid the charge from the opposition that Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill targets institutions run by minorities, especially Christians, Union home ministry asserted Friday that the amendments do not regulate charity but the entry of foreign money into a "sovereign space", which Centre is fully entitled to protect, and emphasised the law at its core is a "national-security" legislation.A team of MHA officials led by home secretary Govind Mohan briefed the joint committee of Parliament - which is scrutinising the bill and held its first meeting - on different facets as it faced questions from MPs, with Mohan insisting the bill is not against any community, sources aware of the details said.He said concerns over national interest, internal security and law and order are the main drivers of the bill. It was introduced by govt in Parliament's budget session and sent to the committee for scrutiny amid stiff protests from opposition parties and Christian groups, who had met home minister Amit Shah to convey their concerns.After the meeting, the panel's chairperson, Sanjay Jaiswal, expressed confidence that it would be able to submit its report in the winter session of Parliament.MPs from BJP-led NDA and opposition parties presented conflicting views.BJP's Nishikant Dubey suggested India had a history of foreign money being used to influence issues of national interest and asked why Ford Foundation was allotted prime property in Lodhi Estate when over 1,400 NGOs linked to foreign funding were closed down under different laws before FCRA was enacted in 1976.Rockefeller Foundation was a key financial support behind an elite cultural and intellectual organisation in central Delhi, he said.Sources said DMK's P Wilson reiterated the charge that the amendments target Christian groups, which make up the majority of religious organisations with an FCRA licence, and was supported by other opposition MPs. Some alleged that these organisations were being targeted as they had empowered Dalits and women in south India.Opposition MPs slammed the proposed amendments as draconian, saying even if an organisation surrendered its FCRA licence, it still allowed assets to be seized.Jaiswal, sources said, flagged protests against the Kudankulam nuclear plant in TN and Sardar Sarovar Dam in Gujarat. BJP circles have argued that foreign-funded NGOs tried to disrupt the two critical projects of national interest under the veneer of environmental concerns.According to data shared by MHA, TN has the highest number of organisations with FCRA registration (2,102), followed by Maharashtra (1,578), Karnataka (1,355) and Delhi (1,218). Foreign contribution increased to Rs 22,974 crore in 2024-25 from Rs 17,832 crore in 2015-16.Out of the total foreign contribution received in 2024-25, 57% (Rs 13,071 crore) was for social purposes, 30% (Rs 6,933 crore) for educational, and only 8% (Rs 11,841 crore) for religious. Under the head of religious purpose, 73% went to Christian groups followed by 17.8% for Hindu organisations, with a little over 1% to Muslims. US and UK at Rs 12,113 crore and Rs 2,414 crore respectively were the two highest contributors.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Wanted: Notorious Lake Tahoe tree poisoner. Reward? $147,000
articles.summary: A question has bedeviled a wealthy Lake Tahoe enclave for years: Who is poisoning the towering trees that stand sentry on the lake's North Shore?
articles.body:
A question has bedeviled a wealthy Lake Tahoe enclave for years: Who is poisoning the towering trees that stand sentry on the North Shore?

Residents of Incline Village, Nev., hope a $147,000 reward will generate some answers.

"It's the most appalling, selfish thing that anyone could do, especially for trees that are irreplaceable," said Chris Nolet, a retired certified public accountant and consultant to the biotechnology industry who assembled a small group of private donors known as Friends of Burnt Cedar Beach to put up the bulk of the reward. "These trees are 100 years old."

The donors are offering $122,000 for information leading to the successful prosecution of anyone responsible. The Incline Village General Improvement District, which owns and manages the residents-only beach where the poisonings took place, has put up another $25,000 and installed additional cameras around the trees.

The move came after an investigation failed to generate actionable leads, Nolet said.

"My feeling is, we've got to try something different," he said, "and money talks."

Someone has, on multiple occasions, slipped into the picturesque wooded cove, drilled holes near the roots of the conifers and poured a chemical inside. A total of 28 trees have been poisoned since 2022 and at least 10 have died, some of them more than a century old.

The attacks escalated this summer, with 16 trees — 13 Jeffrey pines and three white firs — poisoned on three occasions between May and early August. It's too soon to say how many of the trees will survive; some are showing signs of stress including brown needles, according to Sam Gough, an arborist with the Incline Village General Improvement District.

"The effects of chemical exposure may develop slowly and may not become fully apparent for several months or even multiple growing seasons," Gough said Friday at a news conference announcing the reward.

Grounds staff have removed contaminated soil from around the affected trees and applied a biochar and compost mixture to support their natural defensive response, she said. They are also hand-watering the trees to reduce environmental stress and give them a better chance of healing, she said.

Staff will continue regular inspections to detect crown thinning, needle discoloration and loss, reduced growth and abnormal resin production, she said.

"It's a little disheartening to realize that somebody has done something that can't be repaired — like, this damage cannot be repaired," Gough said. "In 150 years, new trees could regrow, but we won't be here for that. It's a great loss."

Six trees were previously poisoned in 2022, four of which died, according to Paul Raymore, a spokesman for the Incline Village General Improvement District. The next year, six more trees were poisoned and survived. But then in 2024, someone re-poisoned those six trees, and they all died, he said.

In the past, diesel fuel was poured around the bases of the trees, and grounds staff said last month that they suspected copper sulfate was dumped into the holes drilled near the roots. The chemical is known to slowly kill trees from the inside out.

Improvement District representatives said Friday that in the most recent incidents staff observed blue granules inside the holes and smelled a strong odor associated with an unidentified liquid, but they declined to speculate on what chemicals may have been used. Soil samples were provided to the sheriff's office in Washoe County, Nev., for analysis, they said.

The sheriff's office did not respond to questions about whether it had received the results of that analysis.

Although investigators haven't determined a motive for the arboreal attacks, both residents and law enforcement officers have theorized they may be the work of a homeowner seeking to improve property value .

Incline Village has earned the nickname "Income Village" due to its reputation as a haven for Silicon Valley's ultrawealthy. Lake views are a hot commodity in the community, and buyers pay steep premiums for properties with unobstructed sightlines.

Still, because the homes are staggered up a hillside, upward of 100 properties could gain a better lake view from the poisoned trees' removal, according to the Washoe County Sheriff's Office.

So far, the most compelling piece of evidence publicly reported by authorities was a flash of light captured by a trail camera about 2 a.m. on Aug 2. Authorities are trying to learn how the perpetrator gained access to the beach, including whether they boated over from the other side of the lake, investigators have said.

The Tahoe Regional Planning Agency is also investigating the tree poisonings. The agency encourages property owners to remove certain trees around homes for defensible-space purposes and works to thin forests throughout the Tahoe Basin to reduce wildfire risk. But healthy, nonhazardous trees are important to the health of Lake Tahoe and environmental quality in the region, according to spokesman Jeff Cowen.

"Root systems protect Lake Tahoe's clarity by stabilizing soils that could erode, and uptaking nutrients that would feed algae in the lake," Cowen wrote in an email. "Healthy forests also provide critical wildlife habitat and protect scenic quality."

Nolet has lived in Incline Village for seven years — part-time for 19 — and describes it as one of the most special places on earth, a veritable paradise where residents can boat, ski, fish and bike.

"The trees are so innocent and that park is so beautiful," he said. "It just kind of is beyond the pale to think that people would sneak in there, drill holes in the trunks, fill them full of poison, put the poison around the tree trunks and sneak out."

"That's an assault on our community that's not acceptable," he added.

The reward funds will be made available to anyone who provides information by March 31 that results in a successful prosecution within two years of the date it is provided.

There's one caveat: neither the person responsible for the poisonings nor any accessories will be eligible for the money. They could face felony charges, as authorities estimate the trees that were killed or damaged to be worth at least $300,000.

Detectives with the Washoe County Sheriff's Office have urged anyone with information, regardless of how insignificant it may seem, to call them at (775) 328-3001 and reference case number 26-4225. Anonymous tips may also be submitted through Secret Witness online or by calling (775) 322-4900.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Ed Sheeran and Macklemore: How a tour spiraled into controversy
articles.summary: Here's what led to the controversy surrounding singer Ed Sheeran's tour and all the twists since rapper Macklemore was dropped over pro-Palestinian comments.
articles.body:
British singer Ed Sheeran is facing growing backlash over a controversial decision to drop rapper Macklemore from the rest of his US tour after Macklemore made pro-Palestinian comments on stage.

The decision - which Sheeran said was made by his promoter, not by himself - has caused ticket sales to decline, supporting acts to drop out, and fans to express frustration.

Sheeran's first show since the debacle began will be on Saturday in Philadelphia, and pro-Palestinian groups are planning to protest outside the venue.

Here's everything you need to know about the controversy.

While performing as the opening act for Sheeran at a concert in early September in New Jersey, Macklemore said: "A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so that I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very, very dear to my heart: Free Palestine."

The Thrift Shop rapper then performed a song dedicated to pro-Palestinian protesters at Columbia University. The lyrics are critical of Israel's military actions in Gaza following the 7 October 2023 Hamas-led attack on Israel.

The following night, Macklemore referred to the death toll as a genocide, a claim that Israel rejects.

In response, the Israeli American Council launched a petition demanding his removal from the tour, and the campaign group StopAntisemitism said the musician had ambushed fans with propaganda.

Pop star Pink, who is Jewish, reposted an anti-Macklemore meme and then her own message, explaining her criticism of the rapper's comments.

Macklemore then posted on Instagram that the media attention "surrounding Pink and what I said" had caused billionaire stadium owner Robert Kraft to call Sheeran.

"Ed told me that Kraft said I would not be allowed to perform in his stadium," Macklemore wrote of Kraft, who also owns the New England Patriots American football team.

Concert promoter Messina Touring Group said Macklemore was dropped because some venues - such as Kraft's Gillette Stadium - would cancel Sheeran's planned concerts if Macklemore remained on the bill.

Kraft, who is Jewish, confirmed he banned the US rapper from performing at Gillette, accusing Macklemore of hate speech and antisemitic rhetoric.

"I agree with Macklemore, too many lives have been lost and there has been too much suffering, but only sharing selective information and ignoring the actions of Hamas is not honest and only advances more divisiveness and hate," Kraft said.

Macklemore was removed from Sheeran's tour on 14 September.

What have Ed Sheeran and Macklemore said?

The rapper said in a lengthy Instagram statement that after a week of "difficult conversations" with Sheeran that ultimately ended "in a place of fundamental disagreement", he was dropped from the lineup.

Sheeran said the call was made by Messina Touring Group. The Bad Habits and Shape of You singer said he respected "Macklemore's strength of purpose to stand up and shout for what he believes", adding that while he doesn't use his own platform for politics, that "doesn't mean I don't care" or "support causes in my own, personal way".

In his statement, Macklemore said he empathised with the difficult position Sheeran was in but criticised the English singer for not taking a stance.

"Taking a side can cost you. Money, brand deals, sponsorships, festivals, private shows, relationships and access. I've lost all of those things. But there is no neutral position between the oppressor and the oppressed," he wrote.

The rapper, who in 2014 apologised for a costume he wore on stage which critics said was anti-Semitic, also addressed the accusations of antisemitism, writing that "one of the most effective ways to enforce silence has been to weaponize the accusation of antisemitism".

In his statement earlier this week, Sheeran said: "There is a reason I do not use my professional platform for politics - my audience includes young people, often children, of all backgrounds."

The singer-songwriter also said he did not want to let down his fans or crew by cancelling the tour.

Sheeran fans and ticket holders are torn about the situation. Some have said that without all the supporting acts, the show is no longer what they paid for.

Damien Given, who is from Northern Ireland and has tickets to Saturday's show, told the BBC that he felt that Macklemore was treated "very, very wrong" and thought Sheeran was not being transparent with fans.

Given said that Sheeran can't suddenly say he's not political because he had previously voiced support for Ukraine after Russia invaded the country.

But another fan named Patti Ann told the BBC that Sheeran was in a "no-win situation".

"I back [Sheeran] 100% for his decision," she said. "I feel like he has an obligation and a contract with his venues, and sometimes, financially, you can't get out of those types of things."

Ticket resale prices for Sheeran's remaining US concert dates have decreased since the controversy began, with some going for below market value.

The controversy has also snowballed into other areas of Sheeran's career. Ireland's Classic Hits Radio announced it was removing Sheeran's music from its playlists because of feedback from listeners who had expressed "disappointment and concern" over his US tour. Sheeran was raised in England but has said he identifies culturally as Irish.

Who were Ed Sheeran's support acts and why did they pull out?

Irish singer-songwriter Aaron Rowe, Danish band Lukas Graham, American singer-songwriter Finneas, and Irish folk band Beoga quit Sheeran's tour following Macklemore's departure.

In a post on Instagram, Rowe thanked Sheeran for the opportunity but said he "cannot stand by and allow billionaires to use their position of power" to silence people who criticise Israel's actions in Gaza. "Free Palestine ," he added.

Lukas Graham similarly thanked Sheeran while expressing support for Palestine and saying the band cannot "carry on with this tour as things stand".

Finneas, the brother of pop star Billie Eilish, said artists should "not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed".

Beoga, which had been serving as Sheeran's backing band, said they support Macklemore's message.

Who will open for Ed Sheeran in Philadelphia?

Sheeran's upcoming concert at Philadelphia's Lincoln Financial Field on Saturday is the first show since Macklemore was dropped from the tour.

There are currently no opening or supporting acts publicly announced for Saturday's show.

Pro-Palestinian groups including Philly Palestine Coalition and Shut Down D&Z are organising a protest on Saturday near the stadium

"There is no neutrality against oppression, only complicity," they said in a post on Instagram.

When are Ed Sheeran's remaining tour dates?

Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour began in January 2026 with shows in New Zealand and Australia before he moved on to the Caribbean, Central America and South America.

On the US and Canadian leg of the tour, which began in Arizona in June, Sheeran has performed in a number of cities including Toronto, Denver, Seattle, Minneapolis and Los Angeles.

After the Philadelphia concert on Saturday, Sheeran has 10 remaining shows in the US through November, including Atlanta and Tampa. He then continues on to South America and wraps up in Mexico in December.

articles.title: US court blocks Trump plan to deport migrants to third countries
articles.summary: US judges affirm migrants must have opportunities to voice safety concerns before deportation to unfamiliar nations.
articles.body:
A US federal appeals court has rejected the Trump administration’s policy of rapidly deporting migrants to countries other than their own – a ruling that could next go before the Supreme Court.

On Friday, a three-judge panel of the 1st US Circuit Court of Appeals in Boston largely upheld a February decision that found the Department of Homeland Security’s so-called third-country removal policy unlawful.

The case stems from a class-action lawsuit testing what due process migrants are owed before being sent to nations with which they have no ties.

Writing for the panel, US Circuit Judge Seth Aframe said migrants must be given a “meaningful” chance to raise safety concerns before removal, rejecting the Trump administration’s narrower reading of the law.

The court did overturn part of the ruling on procedural grounds, concerning whether officials must first try deporting migrants to countries they have ties to.

Trina Realmuto, a lawyer for the plaintiffs at the National Immigration Litigation Alliance, said the decision confirmed that “due process and the protections Congress enacted against persecution and torture cannot be circumvented by putting someone on a plane to a country that was never part of their removal proceedings”.

The DHS did not immediately comment. The Trump administration is expected to appeal the ruling.

Under Trump, the US has struck agreements allowing it to send more than 25,000 migrants to at least 29 third countries, most often Mexico, according to Third Country Deportation Watch, a tracker run by the rights groups Refugees International and Human Rights First.

The policy, adopted in March 2025, allowed removals with only minimal notice if officials had diplomatic assurances against persecution.

The controversial programme has reached the Supreme Court twice.

In 2025, the justices cleared the way for eight men, including nationals of Cuba, Myanmar and Vietnam, to be deported to South Sudan , a country the US State Department advises against visiting because of “crime, kidnapping, and armed conflict”.

The DHS called the removals “a win”, while rights groups said they flouted basic protections.

The Trump administration’s immigration agenda has faced a string of setbacks this month.

A federal judge blocked planned caps on student and journalist visas, calling the government’s justification “exceptionally weak”, while a coalition of 22 states and Washington, DC, sued to stop a separate rule that would let officials deny green cards to immigrants who lawfully use public benefits.

articles.title: Parents could face prison for child's crimes under justice reforms, minister says
articles.summary: The reforms to Parenting Orders could also see parents losing benefits, Jake Richards MP told the Times.
articles.body:
Parents could lose their benefits or face prison sentences for their children's crimes under reforms to the youth justice system, a minister has said.

Youth Justice Minister Jake Richards told the Times newspaper the system "should hold parents to account in a proportionate way for ensuring that they play their role in keeping communities safe".

His comments come after the government set out plans in May to strengthen and expand Parenting Orders, which can currently compel parents or guardians to address their child's behaviour by attending counselling sessions or face fines.

Richards said prison sentences would only apply "in the most extreme cases" and would be up to judges' discretion.

He described the proposed changes in England and Wales as part of a "carrot-and-stick" approach.

"Parenting orders are going to make sure that parents are more involved in the process by which we try to turn around young offenders," Richards told the Times.

"Yes, that will have some stick. It could be custodial, or docking benefits - ultimately it will be up to a judge. But we want them to be more involved and that comes with responsibilities as well."

Critics of the proposals say engaging with parents on a voluntary basis is generally more effective in building trusting relationships and providing support.

Jess Mullen, chief executive of the Alliance for Youth Justice which represents more than 70 organisations that advocate for children, previously questioned how putting parents in prison would provide "stability or support for the child".

When the government white paper was announced in May, then Justice Secretary David Lammy said that strengthening parenting orders would mean "there are real consequences for parents and carers who wilfully fail to support efforts to address their children's behaviour."

He told BBC Breakfast at the time that if a parent was struggling, then the "judge can intervene to make sure that the young person is getting the support that they need and the parent is doing the best that they can".

He also said he expected the power to jail parents to be used "very, very rarely".

Courts are currently required to consider issuing a Parenting Order where a child under 16 has been convicted of an offence.

They can also consider an order for 16 and 17-year-olds if they believe this would help prevent further offences.

The term of the order must not exceed 12 months and breach of a parenting order is a criminal offence with a maximum £1,000 fine, according to the Sentencing Council.

However, government statistics show the use of parenting orders has declined in recent years, from more than 1,000 orders in 2009/10 to just 33 in 2022/23.

The government's youth justice reform plans come after Phase One of the Southport Inquiry report found "catastrophic" failures by the parents of the Southport killer Axel Rudakubana and various agencies meant clear chances to prevent the 2024 child murders were missed.

In the interview with the Times, Richards also rejected calls from lawyers to raise the age of criminal responsibility from 10, saying it would undermine "public faith" in the justice system and it was "not a priority at all".

In June, the Bar Council, the representative body for barristers in England and Wales, said the threshold should rise to 14 due to criminalisation at such an early age not being an "effective, proportionate or just response".

The United Nations has previously pointed out the UK has some of the lowest ages of criminal responsibility in the world and that it should rise it to the UN recommendation of at least 14.

articles.title: North Korea dismisses UN nuclear watchdog resolution
articles.summary: The country rebukes the UN atomic agency’s ‘double standards’ and says nuclear status is ‘irreversible’.
articles.body:
The North Korean Foreign Ministry has dismissed a resolution by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) that criticises Pyongyang’s nuclear weapons programme.

The ministry said on Saturday that its status as a nuclear power is irreversible and backed by its nuclear deterrent, according to a statement released by the state-run Korean Central News Agency (KCNA).

In a separate statement to KCNA, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un’s sister, Kim Yo Jong, accused the nuclear watchdog of double standards.

The IAEA’s “biased viewpoint and double standards” are “the fundamental factor causing the collapse of the international nuclear non-proliferation system”, she said.

Kim Yo Jong said the UN nuclear watchdog had turned a blind eye to the “blatant nuclear proliferation activities” of the United States and South Korea’s “nuclear submarine introduction plan”, while the agency forcibly adopted a resolution against North Korea’s “self-defensive and legitimate nuclear activities”.

The North Korean Foreign Ministry also accused “hostile forces” of seeking to bring an end to the country’s nuclear programme during this week’s general conference of the IAEA.

“Pitifully, the ‘resolution’ cooked up by the US and the West has no effect on the DPRK’s position as a nuclear weapons state,” a foreign ministry spokesperson said, referring to the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea, its official name.

The state media also reported that Kim Jong Un carried out a three-day inspection tour of major munitions factories this week.

Analysts say North Korea has been overhauling its military with Russian help since the two countries signed a mutual defence treaty in 2024. They say combat experience gained by Pyongyang’s troops deployed to the war in Ukraine has also aided the effort.

Kim Jong Un also gave a lecture to a propaganda workers’ training session in Pyongyang on Friday, KCNA reported, telling attendees modern “ideological warfare” needed to be innovative, creative and aggressive rather than repeating old methods.

While Kim Yo Jong rebuked what she called double standards favouring the US and South Korea, both countries have recently said they want to improve relations with North Korea.

On Friday, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said that US President Donald Trump wants dialogue with Pyongyang, and Seoul will work to facilitate potential talks.

Trump, seeking to revive the bond he forged with Kim Jong Un in his first term, said last month that he plans to meet the North Korean leader later this year.

The US president said it was important to “get along” with Kim, adding that Pyongyang now had 57 “very powerful” nuclear weapons.

articles.title: Asia’s fruit wars: The secretive world of plant invention and seed smuggling
articles.summary: The fruit hanging on the branch looks tantalizingly good – round and plump, with a fragrant, deep orange skin.
articles.body: The fruit hanging on the branch looks tantalizingly good – round and plump, with a fragrant, deep orange skin. But this isn’t just any fruit. The Beni Princess is a prized citrus with a signature jelly-like texture and sweet juice that took 20 years to develop by crossbreeding two elite varieties. Creating new varieties of fruit is a lucrative business, and Japan’s luxury cultivars often command whopping prices. So when Ehime prefecture in the country’s southwest proudly unveiled the Beni Princess last year, orchardists saw opportunity. On their five-acre family farm, Ryohei Mori and his wife Kyeong-hui Choi had around 200 trees of another citrus variety ripped up so they could plant the Beni Princess –– even taking out a loan to build new facilities. “It costs an absolute fortune at first. Buying the saplings, building the greenhouses, and everything,” Mori said. The return may be worth the investment when they begin selling the first batches next spring. The only problem? Chinese farmers might beat them to it – and without permission, according to Japanese media reports. Choi said she was appalled at the prospect the fruit might have been “stolen,” but said she was resigned to the fact there was nothing they could do besides hope that Japan’s government might act. It can take years of tedious research and testing to develop new crops –– to ensure not only that they taste good, but also that they can grow at scale. The development costs can be eye-watering. Just like other types of intellectual property (IP), fruit varieties can be proprietary and protected by law. But while you can report copyright infringement for a movie or a song, it’s much harder to prevent people from taking and planting seeds. That has spawned a shadow war involving seed espionage and sapling smuggling across Asia – which experts say not only hurts farmers and breeders, but also stymies much-needed innovation as climate change threatens food security. The Beni Princess appears to have been the latest target, with reports that seedlings are being sold on Chinese e-commerce sites – while its application for IP protection is still pending. CNN couldn’t independently verify the claims, but the speculation prompted a plea from Ehime’s governor for Tokyo to investigate. Norikazu Suzuki, Japan’s agriculture minister, has called the issue “particularly serious.” A major fruit innovator, Japan has been burned before by seed copycats. After it debuted the Shine Muscat grape in the early 2000s, Japan naively failed to register the fruit – highly coveted for its floral scent and juiciness – for protection in overseas markets. A deadline passed, then it was too late; now, Chinese and South Korean farms grow and sell the Shine Muscat in huge quantities and at a steep discount. The price difference is evident during a quick stop at Hong Kong supermarkets – with Chinese Shine Muscats selling at 1/20th the cost of their Japanese equivalent. Suzuki estimated that Japan misses out on 20 billion yen ($126.9 million) every year in lost royalties due to the licensing mistake. The lost revenue is a concern for Shinya Sato, a grower in Japan’s central Yamanashi prefecture who depends on Shine Muscats and other grape varieties for his livelihood. “I want people to enjoy eating what I grow, and I want to be fairly compensated for my labor,” he said. “Everyone works hard to build up that value and make something delicious.” How do you steal a seed? There’s no simple way to protect a plant variety across borders. Protection laws vary by country – for instance, a breeder in Japan who wants to prevent their unique variety from being copied in China or South Korea would need to apply for protection separately in those countries. And what legally counts as infringement in one country might not count in another. But several governments across Asia have tightened their regulations in recent years, making it easier for breeders to protect their varieties, said David Jefferson, an associate professor at the University of Canterbury in New Zealand who specializes in environmental and intellectual property law. China has strengthened its seed protection laws several times in the last few years; similarly, Japan passed new legislation in July to prevent the illicit export of homegrown varieties. And increasingly, Jefferson said, countries are adjusting their laws to move closer to a global standard set by the International Union for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants (UPOV), which has 80 member states. But UPOV is not an enforcement agency. So when a plant gets stolen, smuggled out of the country, and grown elsewhere without permission, it’s up to the breeder to stop it – by proving through genetic testing that the replicated fruit in question is the proprietary variety, and going to law enforcement. That’s a daunting task for smaller institutions like university research labs or think tanks that lack the resources to track down seed smugglers and prove their case. But large multinational companies, whose original varieties are fiercely protected, have had some success. In 2011, Iowa farmers found a Chinese national on his knees in a cornfield, digging through the soil. He fled, and the ensuing FBI investigation unraveled a long-running conspiracy to steal genetically modified corn seeds and ship them to China. The thief, Mo Hailong, was sentenced in 2016 to 36 months in prison for conspiracy to steal trade secrets from DuPont Pioneer and Monsanto, two of the world’s largest seed companies at the time. He was scheduled to be deported after being released. That same year, the world’s biggest seller of kiwifruit, New Zealand-based Zespri, hired private investigators to dig into rumors that its Sungold variety was being illegally grown and sold in China. This was a big deal; years earlier, Zespri had specifically created the sweeter golden kiwifruit to be resistant to a disease that had ravaged kiwifruit orchards around the world. The new variety helped the industry recover from the disease, and was a windfall for Zespri, which registered the fruit as its exclusive property in many countries including China. The smuggler, Chinese national Gao Haoyu, owned a Sungold orchard in New Zealand and was licensed to grow and sell the variety there – but he secretly took young branches to China and sold them to farmers there. Before long, the Sungold variety had been illegally planted on more than 200 hectares in Hubei province and sold online. After a protracted legal battle, a New Zealand court ordered Gao to pay Zespri $8.8 million in damages in 2020. And last year, a Chinese court ordered him to remove all Sungold orchards in China and to pay Zespri nearly $780,000. CNN attempted to contact Gao through the last publicly available email and phone number associated with his New Zealand business. We did not hear back. But, in interviews with Chinese media, he has claimed that his motives were altruistic. “99% of kiwifruit growers in China support me,” he told Chinese outlet Caixin in 2021. “I just wanted to contribute to the Chinese people by bringing the varieties over for everyone to grow, but I never made money from the varieties.” What’s at stake? Gao isn’t the only one who’s made this argument. Mo, the corn seed thief, also argued that corn was a public good, according to “The Scientist and the Spy,” a book by journalist Mara Hvistendahl on the case. Other critics argue that food shouldn’t be controlled by large agricultural corporations, and that plant variety protection laws disempower local and indigenous communities. Jefferson, the professor, acknowledged these real concerns, especially among developing nations in South and Southeast Asia, and Sub-Saharan Africa. But, he said, under most laws, breeders have to be able to prove that their creations are new and improved in some way to be registered for protection. And, he said, these laws are necessary because the unauthorized spread of newly developed varieties can cause widespread harm. For one, it drives down the overall price of the crop. Take Shine Muscat grapes: “Once known to be one of the prized varieties, it now produces nothing for farmers,” said Minori Hagiwara, who chairs a UPOV subcommittee and works in Japan’s Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries. These premium fruits also often require methodical techniques to ensure their signature characteristics, like the precise amount of sunlight or the timing of pruning. But illicit growers are likely to churn out lower-quality fruit sold under the same name. “It really doesn’t reward the farmers who put in effort,” Hagiwara said. It’s not just growers at risk from seed smuggling; when original varieties are protected and licensed, it creates a whole supply chain of exporters and distributors who are all impacted by illicit distribution. The broader concern, though, is stifling innovation. When there’s rampant stealing of new varieties, countries will invest less in research and development because there’s no guarantee they’ll earn it back. Japan, for instance, is targeted heavily in fruit theft because it produces so many “premium” products – and it’s now spending less each year creating new varieties, potentially threatening its competitive edge in the market, Hagiwara said. Climate change raises the stakes –– with yields of some traditional staple crops, like rice, already plummeting in places like Vietnam and Thailand. Crop innovation is seen as critical to guaranteeing long-term food supplies. Vietnam, a UPOV member, has enthusiastically invested in creating new, resilient rice varieties –– and their yield has begun to increase in recent years, Hagiwara said. Meanwhile neighboring Thailand, with weaker variety protection laws, continues to see yields tank. One of UPOV’s key goals is to create a universal patent, so that with one application, a breeder can get worldwide protection, she added. But it’s still a far-off dream. In the meantime, farmers do their best to beef up security – hyperaware that all someone needs to do is cut off a branch from their trees for it to be smuggled away, draining their profits from some distant orchard in another country. Sato, the Shine Muscat grape grower, said when his father owned the farm, there were no security measures. Now, he keeps defensive netting around his vines during harvest season to deter thieves. But he can only do so much. “There’s stealing directly from the field, but there’s also stealing our brand value, taking it and pretending they built it themselves,” he said.

articles.title: These Israelis want to fly home to vote. Netanyahu is trying to stop them
articles.summary: With only a matter of weeks until Israel heads to the ballot box, the sharpest political battleground is unfolding up above (or “in the skies”).
articles.body: With only a matter of weeks until Israel heads to the ballot box, the sharpest political battleground is unfolding in the skies. Tens of thousands of Israelis living abroad are reportedly booking flights home to vote - and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party is trying to keep at least some of them grounded. On Wednesday, Likud filed a petition asking Israel’s Central Elections Committee to block “Fly & Vote,” a grassroots initiative helping Israeli expatriates fly home for election day. Likud accused it of being an illegal, foreign funded operation, claiming it could “severely harm the integrity of the election.” In a country where razor-thin margins often decide the outcome of an election, these votes could play a major part in determining the country’s next leader. Unlike most Western democracies in which citizens abroad can mail in a ballot, Israel doesn’t allow absentee voting; only diplomats and official envoys can vote from outside the country. Ordinary citizens abroad - up to 10% of the population at any given time - must return home or forfeit their right to vote. Adi Ayash, an Israeli digital content creator who lives in Thailand, said there was never a question about returning to vote. “As someone who is very engaged and very worried by the reality of the (current) Israeli leadership, I feel that it is my duty,” he told CNN. “Not to exercise my democratic right because of flight costs or convenience feels to me like extreme hypocrisy.” The October 27 vote will be the first national election after four turbulent years under Netanyahu’s right-wing, ultra-Orthodox coalition, a term which included mass protests of liberal Israelis against a judicial overhaul and the October 7 attack in 2023 which was followed by a three-year multi-front war. According to the latest polls, both Netanyahu’s coalition and his deeply fragmented opposition are falling short of the 61-seat majority needed to form a government. Likud fears an influx of Israeli expats could help the opposition parties in a close election. “Fly & Vote” was launched by the America-Israel Democracy AID Coalition, a US-based nonprofit founded in 2023 that describes its mission as “strengthening Israel’s democratic foundations.” The group says it doesn’t pay directly for anyone’s travel but uses technology to search commercial listings for affordable, creative flight routes and group rates. It also helps with logistics like renewing passports, checking eligibility, and organizing charter flights if demand warrants or commercial options fall short. The group says more than 35,000 Israelis have registered, and internal surveys suggest over 50,000 intend to return to vote. “Something bigger is happening here. There is an international movement from all over the world. It’s a national event,” said Batell Blaish Sultanik, co-founder of “Fly & Vote,” comparing it to the wave of citizens who returned to enlist after October 7. “Israelis understand their vote is important,” Sultanik added. She insists the effort is nonpartisan and that no participant receives money or benefits from the group. “We do not ask or check who they are voting for behind the ballot box,” she told CNN. “It’s about the right to vote.” Netanyahu’s Likud party, however, disagrees. In its petition, the party says the coalition is a political body, created to channel American donations to Israeli protest groups. Likud claims it is tied to the opposition Democrats party. The group and the party deny any affiliation. Even if participants pay for their own tickets, the Likud argues priority flight access and group discount rates are prohibited benefits that amount to election bribery under Israeli law. The petition also points to a separate AID coalition project, called “FLY AND AID,” which offers $250 gift cards for volunteering in Israel. “This is a distinctly political body attempting to influence the election system,” the petition states. The Likud’s efforts have only increased the resolve of some Israelis to return for the election. Josh Drill, who will fly from New York with a “Fly & Vote” group, told CNN: “Every attempt to obstruct our democratic right to vote only strengthens our determination to get on a plane, cast our ballot, and take part in this election to help shape the future of Israel.” The outcome of the Likud petition hinges on evidence, said Guy Lurie, a research fellow at the Israel Democracy Institute. “It depends on facts and evidence that will be presented to the Central Elections Committee. The central legal question is whether organizing flights - without directly funding - amounts to a prohibited benefit and whether Likud can substantiate its claims that the initiative amounts to a foreign legal activity,” he said. The AID coalition insists it operates within the law and serves all Israelis abroad. “The Likud seeks to prevent Israeli citizens who boarded planes after October 7, tax-paying citizens who want to be involved in their homeland, from the right and the obligation to take part in deciding the future of the state of Israel,” the group said in a statement. Opposition figures have raised a separate concern: Likud’s control over the Transportation Ministry and the Airport Authority, floating scenarios in which flight slots are restricted or disrupted around election day. A July report in Haaretz suggested internal ministry discussions about scaling back activities on October 27, prompting lawmakers and the Israeli Association for Civil Rights to ask the Central Election Committee to guarantee the skies remain open and flights continue uninterrupted. “Reducing the ability to travel from abroad to reach Israel to vote is a serious violation of freedom of voting and the most basic democratic mechanism,” the opposition Yesh Atid party wrote in an appeal. Transportation Minister Miri Regev, from Likud, dismissed the report as a “gross lie.” “I kept the skies open throughout the war,” she said in a video posted on social media. “Does anyone really think I’m going to close the skies on election day? And besides, who said that only leftists travel abroad and return on election day?” Notably, ultra-Orthodox voters have traditionally flown home en masse - largely from New York - without similar objections, and the Likud has previously promoted legislation to enable external voting from abroad. This time is different. Far-right Communications Minister Shomo Karhi recently said in a radio interview that Israelis abroad who wish to influence the country’s future should immigrate. “Whoever does not live here should not come just because in the name of the ‘Just Not Bibi’ – to try to replace the government,” he said.
